newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fourteen killed in Colombia commuter plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Fourteen killed in Colombia commuter plane crash.

text.p: A small commuter plane ploughed into a mountain on the outskirts of this city in northwest Colombia Saturday, killing all but one of the 15 people aboard, authorities said.

Civil Aviation officials said the plane, a Canadian-built Twin Otter belonging to Colombia's Aces airline, crashed into the tree-lined Padre Amaya mountain southwest of the city and burst into flames shortly after takeoff from the Enrique Olaya Herrera airport.

It had been headed for the Bahia Solano beach resort on Colombia's Pacific coast. It was carrying 13 passengers and two crew members when it went down for unknown reasons in fair weather, the officials said.
"We don't know what happened, all we know is that it crashed," one Civil Aviation official told reporters.
"We've been in touch with the control tower and apparently the pilot never reported any emergency," he added.

Two survivors of the crash were rushed to Medellin's Las Vegas hospital with multiple fractures and burns over up to 90 percent of their bodies. However, one of them, identified as 15-year-old Olga Lucia Moreno, died of her injuries shortly afterward, hospital officials said.
The only other survivor, Pedro Rafael Rojas, was in critical condition, the officials said.

All of the victims, including Aces pilot Juan Carlos Bermudez, were believed to be Colombian nationals. But Hector Suarez, regional chief of the Civil Aviation Authority, said a complete passanger list had not been made available as of late Saturday afternoon.

Olaya Herrera has been described by pilots as among Latin America's most dangerous airports. It is nestled into a relatively narrow valley ringed by steep mountains and access to its landing strip can force larger aircraft to engage in a series of corkscrew-like turns.
